title: Windows Server 2028 preview ships hardened by default and asks admins to keep up
summary: Microsoft used Ignite to open the Windows Server 2028 public preview, whose Server Core install arrives with hundreds of security settings already on: Kerberos ahead of NTLM, extra protections around LSASS, modern-only TLS ciphers, hybrid post-quantum key exchange built on ML-KEM and restricted remote desktop defaults. Microsoft says the baseline follows DISA STIG guidance, and administrators can still re-enable features. The cost is compatibility with legacy protocols and older management tools, and the hardening applies to new installations only.
